search-nc.name: Web search summaries on the North Coast AVA
search-nc.note: Several pages agree on the six counties and on 1983. Used only to cross-check Wikipedia.

claims.claim: The North Coast AVA was established in 1983.
claims.note: Wikipedia says 24 September. Other pages say 21 September. Not checked against the TTB, so only the year is used.

claims.claim: It covers six counties north of San Francisco: Lake, Marin, Mendocino, Napa, Solano and Sonoma.
claims.quote: Lake, Marin, Mendocino, Napa, Solano, and Sonoma

claims.claim: It is a very large AVA, over 3 million acres or about 4,700 square miles.
The climate is maritime, shaped by fog and breezes from the Pacific. It spans a wide range of climate regions, from I to IV.
claims.quote: affected by the fog and breezes from the Pacific Ocean

claims.claim: It contains many smaller AVAs, including Napa Valley, Alexander Valley, Russian River Valley, Anderson Valley and Dry Creek Valley.
The name North Coast first meant three counties: Napa, Sonoma and Mendocino. Lake, Marin and Solano were added during the 1980s approval.
claims.note: Search summary of a Federal Register based source. Not read directly.

claims.claim: Many grapes grow here, including Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Zinfandel and Sauvignon Blanc.
A North Coast label lets a winery blend fruit from several counties and sub-AVAs.
claims.note: Follows from the AVA covering six counties. Not stated by a source read.

conflicts: Established: 21 September 1983 (several pages) against 24 September 1983 (Wikipedia). Year only is used.
